problem:
Calculate the points where the ellipse 
$\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{16}+\frac{(y+3)^{2}}{12}=1$ intercepts the $y$-axis.
worked_solution:
To calculate the $y$-intercept, we need to substitute $x=0$ in the equation of the ellipse and solve the resulting equation for $y.$ Doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x-2)^{2}}{16}+\frac{(y+3)^{2}}{12} & =1 \\ \frac{(0-2)^{2}}{16}+\frac{(y+3)^{2}}{12} & =1 \\ \frac{4}{16}+\frac{(y+3)^{2}}{12} & =1 \\ \frac{1}{4}+\frac{(y+3)^{2}}{12} & =1 \\ 3+(y+3)^{2} & =12 \\ (y+3)^{2} & =9 \\ y+3 & =\pm 3 \\ y & =-3\pm 3 \\ y & =-6\,,0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the ellipse intercepts the $y$-axis at the points $(0,-6)$ and $(0,0).$
